title: Grieg plays his wedding march
work: Wedding Day at Troldhaugen, Op. 65 No. 6
question: How differently do Grieg and Harald Vetter make this wedding march dance?
intro: More guests than expected arrived at Troldhaugen for Edvard and Nina Grieg’s silver wedding on 11 June 1892. Four years later, Grieg remembered the occasion in a piano piece, Wedding Day at Troldhaugen. His own 1903 disc squeezes the party into two minutes; Harald Vetter plays the complete piece.

recordings.label: Edvard Grieg
recordings.note: The composer plays his own abridged version in Paris in 1903, with the march packed onto a short disc.

recordings.label: Harald Vetter
recordings.note: The complete piece, recorded on 4 October 2006, includes the quiet middle section and the march’s return.

passages.label: The march steps out
passages.note: Low octaves and clipped chords give the march its tread. Little triplets send the right hand skipping into the next phrase.

passages.label: The piano grows bolder
passages.note: The march gathers strength, with firmer bass notes beneath the right hand’s chords.

passages.label: Full chords
passages.note: The piano fills out the march in emphatic chords, keeping the short, lively figures between its heavier beats.

alignment.scope: Shared opening material only; the complete source recordings remain unedited. No whole-work tempo ratio.
alignment.note: An exploratory 4–94 / 5–120 second map had low-confidence opening points and a plateau near reference 90–91.5 seconds. Inspection against the measured 46/62-second and 74/98-second changes supported the shared passage but not the shortened ending. The published map excludes both uncertain ends; its remaining path was inspected and has no point below 0.8. No pitch transposition or audio edit was applied.
